title: What is a responsible manager?
description: A responsible manager is a person nominated to show a licensee has the knowledge and skills to provide its services. How ASIC RG 105 sets the competence test.
shortAnswer: A responsible manager is a person a financial services or credit licensee nominates to its regulator as having direct responsibility for significant day to day decisions about its licensed services, and whose knowledge and skills demonstrate the licensee's organizational competence. The term is used by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), whose Regulatory Guide 105 sets five options for showing a responsible manager is competent, built on qualifications and recent relevant experience.
keyTakeaways: Responsible managers are how an Australian financial services licensee shows it meets the organizational competence obligation in section 912A(1)(e) of the Corporations Act 2001.
ASIC RG 105 sets five options combining qualifications and relevant experience; most require three years of relevant experience in the past five.
ASIC expects at least two responsible managers and no more than 20 nominated at any time.
Competence must be reviewed regularly and maintained, with records kept, not established once at licensing.
From 16 October 2026, responsible managers who are also Financial Accountability Regime accountable persons face reduced evidence requirements on the ASIC Regulatory Portal.

sections.heading: What does a responsible manager do?

blocks.text: A responsible manager makes or directly oversees the significant day to day decisions about the financial services or credit activities a licensee provides. Their knowledge and skills are the evidence that the licensee as a whole is competent to provide those services.

[RG 105 Licensing: Organisational competence](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-105-licensing-organisational-competence/), issued on 23 June 2022, explains how ASIC assesses the obligation in section 912A(1)(e) of the Corporations Act 2001 to maintain the competence to provide the licensed financial services. RG 105 does not cover the separate obligation in section 912A(1)(f) to ensure representatives are adequately trained, which is addressed in other guidance such as [RG 146](/regulations/asic-rg-146-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How does a responsible manager show competence under RG 105?

blocks.text: A responsible manager shows competence through one of five options in Table 1 of [RG 105](https://download.asic.gov.au/media/cndf2udp/rg105-published-23-june-2022-20250616.pdf), each combining qualifications with relevant experience. The table summarizes the experience element; the guide sets out the qualification level for each option.

blocks.text: RG 105 also notes that the former ASIC Training Register was valid up to 24 September 2012 and is no longer current, so older references to registered courses need checking against the current options.

sections.heading: What must a licensee do after nominating responsible managers?

blocks.text: The licensee must keep its responsible managers competent, review their competence regularly and when the business changes, and keep records. RG 105 links this to condition 4 of the standard license conditions in Pro Forma 209.

items: Nominate at least two responsible managers; ASIC allows up to 20 at any time (RG 105.49 to 105.50).
Match each responsible manager's competence to the specific products and services they oversee.
Review competence regularly and when services, products or people change.
Maintain knowledge through ongoing training and development.
Keep records of the assessment, the review and the training.
Notify ASIC of changes; if a responsible manager is named as a key person in condition 3 of Pro Forma 209, changes require a license variation.

blocks.text: A [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) mapped to the license authorizations makes these reviews faster, because a new product or authorization shows which responsible manager competencies need checking. The detail is on [ASIC RG 105 organizational competence](/regulations/asic-rg-105-organisational-competence).

sections.heading: Do credit licensees need responsible managers?

blocks.text: Yes. Australian credit licensees also nominate responsible managers, under [RG 206](https://download.asic.gov.au/media/gmcnpijx/rg206-published-1-april-2020-20221025.pdf). ASIC expects them to have two years of relevant problem free experience and a Certificate IV level credit qualification or higher, and to complete at least 20 hours of continuing professional development each year.

sections.heading: How does a responsible manager compare with similar roles?

blocks.text: A responsible manager supplies a licensee's competence; an [accountable person](/glossary/accountable-person) carries personal accountability for an area; and [fit and proper](/glossary/fit-and-proper) is a test of competence and character. Other markets meet the same need differently: the Dubai Financial Services Authority, for example, requires certain functions to be held by approved Authorised Individuals, and EU banking rules assess key function holders for suitability. ASIC has said changes for responsible managers who are also FAR accountable persons took effect on its Regulatory Portal on 16 October 2026, with an updated RG 105 expected in the first quarter of 2027.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each license authorization to the competencies a responsible manager needs, links each competence to evidence of qualifications, experience and ongoing development, and shows where a change of product or authorization leaves a gap. That keeps the RG 105 record current between licensing events.

faqs.q: How many responsible managers does a licensee need?
faqs.a: ASIC expects at least two responsible managers and allows a maximum of 20 nominated at any time (RG 105.49 to 105.50). Under RG 105.51 it may accept only one, for example for a one person advisory business or where the main business is not financial services.

faqs.q: Can an individual licensee be their own responsible manager?
faqs.a: Yes, and RG 105.50 says they must be. An individual who holds or applies for an Australian financial services license in their own name must nominate themselves as the responsible manager, and their own qualifications and experience must meet one of the RG 105 options.

faqs.q: What happens if a licensee loses a responsible manager?
faqs.a: The licensee must still meet the organizational competence obligation, so it should nominate a suitable replacement and notify ASIC. Where the person is a key person under condition 3 of Pro Forma 209, the change also requires a license variation. Failing the obligation can lead to administrative action.

faqs.q: Is responsible manager the same as a responsible manager for representative training?
faqs.a: No. Responsible managers demonstrate the licensee's organizational competence under section 912A(1)(e). Training of representatives who give advice is a separate obligation under section 912A(1)(f), covered by other ASIC guidance and the financial adviser education standards.
